hardware.pose_tol.measured_on: decided: the tolerance of a pose check in one project
hardware.pose_tol.description: a pose joint farther than this from its reference value is not at zero

rules.title: Bought parts come from their real model
rules.statement: Every bought part this part touches is modelled from its STEP file with the owner's measurements applied, not as a box. Thread sizes, hole patterns, connectors and the room a plug needs are read from the model and measured on the part.
rules.why: A motor drawn as a plain box hid its connector: a large printed part was scrapped. A magnet pocket was cut for a magnet the owner never had, and a board mount was guessed from a photo.

attest.question: Which bought parts does this part touch, and is each one from its STEP file with measured sizes?
labels: every bought part it touches is from its STEP file, measured sizes applied

rules.title: Every fastener feature has its ref body
rules.statement: Every fastener feature of a printed part has its named reference body: a screw (head and shank), an insert, a washer, a dowel, a bearing, in a hardware component that belongs to that part. No orphans. The length in a name is the modelled length. When a hole moves, its refs are rebuilt in the same pass. Purchase lists and build notes are made from the refs.
rules.why: Six refs were named 2 to 6 mm shorter than the screw the stack needed, so a parts list made from the names would have bought the wrong screws. Changes repeatedly ended with "hardware refs not updated". The screw and washer checks see only fasteners that have a ref body: a hole without one passes them in silence.
fix_order: Rebuild the refs of the part from its holes before the gate run.
Remove refs whose hole is gone.

attest.question: Does every screw hole, insert pocket and washer landing of this part have its ref body, rebuilt after the last change of a hole?
labels: every fastener feature of this part has its ref body, rebuilt after the last hole change
this part has no fastener features
some refs are missing or stale: listed in the report for the owner

auto.label: this part has no fastener features

rules.note: A question until a judge reads the census: a classified screw hole or insert pocket with nothing on its axis. See also access.screws_modelled_first. Which part a ref belongs to is assembly.hardware_owner. The label "no fastener features" is refused while the screw probe lists a screw, a washer, a screw hole or an insert pocket on the part. A ref that is there and that no probe recognised is hardware.recognised.

rules.title: What sits in a screw hole is recognised
rules.statement: Every bought body on the axis of a screw hole or an insert pocket of the part is recognised: as the screw of that hole (a head on a shank, one body or two), or as a washer, an insert, a nut, a bearing, a dowel or a pin. A hole with a bought body on its axis that nothing recognised, and no recognised screw there, means the screw probe may be blind to the naming of this document: no screw rule has looked at that hole, and "this part has no screws" is not proven. The check is then not run; it never fails a part. A name picks the candidates and the geometry decides: a body that a name pattern picked and that is no such thing by its shape (a magnet in a component "screws and magnets") is listed, not judged.
rules.why: A plate with nine screws came back with no screw at all: each screw was modelled as two bodies, head and shank, named by thread and standard with no word "screw". Every screw rule passed in silence. A disc magnet in a hardware component was judged as an M6 screw, and a clamp screw named after the bearing it clamps was judged as that bearing.
fix_order: Name the screw ref as a screw is named (thread and length, "M3x12", or the word screw), or set screws.ref_pattern to the naming of the document, and run the gate again.
Model the screw as a head on a shank on one axis, one body or two bodies of one component.
A pin, a dowel, a magnet or a shaft in a hole of screw size: name it for what it is (pin, dowel) so that it is not taken for a missed screw.
A screw hole whose screw is not modelled yet: place the ref (hardware.refs_present).
rules.note: The screw probe writes "fastener_holes": every clearance hole, counterbore, countersink and insert pocket of the census with the recognised screw on its axis and the bought bodies on its axis that nothing recognised. Facts of an older probe are compared through the census. The verdict is NOT_RUN, never FAIL: what a probe did not recognise is no measured defect.

rules.title: Ref bodies are never printed and never cut
rules.statement: Reference bodies never sit in a printed part's own component, never cut a part and are skipped by every exporter. A superseded part is removed from the model and from the exports in the same pass.
rules.why: A superseded base part stayed on a production plate until the owner noticed it.
rules.note: The gate lists printed parts and refs apart (the not_printed patterns of gate/project.json), and an STL that matches no current part is a row of project.stl_without_stamp.

rules.title: One appearance per hardware type
rules.statement: Each hardware type has its own appearance: each insert length its colour, screws, washers and dowels theirs. After any edit of a hardware component the colours are audited, because a base-feature edit resets them.
rules.why: Inserts turned grey after an edit, twice, and two insert lengths could no longer be told apart in the build pictures. The owner caught both.

rules.title: Hardware is found by geometry, not by an exact name
rules.statement: A hardware check finds parts by their geometry, not by an exact name: a copy suffix or a renamed body must not hide a fastener. A change applied to "all screws" is followed by an audit that counts every head.
rules.why: Six heads that carried the copy suffix "(1)" were skipped by a script that matched names: only 3 of the 4 screws of one joint were changed.
rules.note: The ref patterns (screws.ref_pattern, washers.ref_pattern, bearings.ref_pattern) are name filters. Set them to the project's naming and compare the count a probe reports with the hardware list.

rules.title: The model is in its reference pose
rules.statement: The model is in its reference pose, every pose joint at 0 within {hardware.pose_tol}, before save, export and checks.
rules.why: No failed print behind it. The checks that measure in the pose as modelled (openings, gaps to neighbours) answer for the pose they find.

rules.title: Use what the owner has
rules.statement: Hardware and bought parts come from what the owner has and from standard sizes in stock first: nothing cut to length, nothing made to order. Before a purchase is proposed, the photo of the lot and its form factor are checked.
rules.why: Idlers were put into a cart although the owner had bearings that did the job, and rods were chosen that needed cutting.
